2609.05151.title: Large Language Models with At Most One Spike per Neuron
2609.05151.paper_summary: Leveraging their inherent sparse event-driven computation, spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a promising path toward energy-efficient large language models (LLMs). Time-to-first-spike (TTFS) coding generates at most one spike per neuron within a time window, yielding extremely low firing rates. However, conventional TTFS SNNs are restricted to specific structures, making it challenging to encode certain blocks in LLM -- such as layer normalization and matrix multiplication --using TTFS. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a reference-based strategy specifically to encode the four core LLM components: embedding layers, layer normalization, attention-related operations and dropout. We construct a fully TTFS-based SNN architecture and train it end-to-end. Experiments on modern LLMs like BERT and GPT-2 demonstrate that our approach achieves performance comparable to ANN counterparts on natural language understanding and common-sense reasoning, while a clear gap remains on language modeling perplexity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to scale a spiking LLM to 1.5 billion parameters using TTFS coding. We also report an estimate of spike-related energy; this is a spike-count proxy under an established cost model rather than a measurement on neuromorphic hardware.
2609.05151.paper_summary_zh: 利用其固有的稀疏事件驅動計算，尖峰神經網絡（SNNs）提供了一條朝向節能的大型語言模型（LLMs）的有希望的道路。首次尖峰時間（TTFS）編碼在一個時間窗口內每個神經元最多生成一個尖峰，產生極低的發射率。然而，傳統的TTFS SNNs受到特定結構的限制，使得使用TTFS編碼某些LLM中的特定模塊（如層正規化和矩陣乘法）變得具有挑戰性。為了克服這一限制，我們提出了一種基於參考的策略，專門用於編碼四個核心LLM組件：嵌入層、層正規化、與注意力相關的操作和丟棄。 我們構建了一個完全基於TTFS的SNN架構並進行端到端訓練。對現代LLM（如BERT和GPT-2）的實驗表明，我們的方法在自然語言理解和常識推理方面達到了可與ANN對應物相媲美的性能，但在語言建模困惑度上仍然存在明顯的差距。據我們所知，這是第一個使用TTFS編碼將尖峰LLM擴展到15億參數的工作。我們還報告了與尖峰相關的能量估算；這是在一個既定成本模型下的尖峰計數代理，而不是在神經形態硬體上的測量。
